title: PMOS bias reference
description: A PMOS bias line drawn as a circuit: a diode-connected PMOS hanging from the supply port, with its programmed current sunk to ground by an ideal current source. The programmed current is the one current typed here. The device's drain is its gate, so its $V_{DS}$ is its own $V_{GS}$ and the table is read along that diagonal with nothing estimated. A PMOS on the gate wire at K times this width and at this length copies the current density, and so carries K times the programmed current less its drain-voltage error. At a low inversion level the same diode is the simplest cascode gate bias, one strong-inversion $|V_{GS}|$ below the supply. The sheet publishes the gate wire's level above ground, $V_b$, and its width, gate-source voltage and current. A composing sheet maps the supply port to its supply and the gate port to the gate wire, and passes in its supply, its own programmed current, length and inversion level. The ideal source stands for whatever generates the reference current, which this sheet does not draw. Used alone, the sheet sizes the reference at the values typed here.

params.name: I_ref
params.note: the programmed reference current, sunk from the diode by the ideal source

params.name: L_ref
params.note: the reference's length. A mirror copies a current density at one length, so a composing sheet gives its mirror outputs the same one

params.name: gm_id_ref
params.note: inversion level of the reference: it sets how far below the supply the gate wire sits, and every mirror output on it inherits it

equations.name: V_b
equations.note: the level of the gate wire above ground: the supply less the diode's drop
